About us

IntelFinder is a pioneering SaaS solution that delivers fully automated, scalable, and customer-specific threat intelligence. Our mission is to democratize threat intelligence and digital brand protection by offering comprehensive detection of external threats at an affordable rate. Designed for ease of use, IntelFinder requires minimal training, empowering all users, from cyber security professionals to even those without a security background, to effectively detect and respond to threats pertinent to their business. Key features of IntelFinder include: - Affordability: Cost-effective and straightforward pricing ensures that robust cybersecurity is accessible to organizations of all sizes. - Accessibility: User-friendly interface and straightforward alerts enable seamless integration into your operations, regardless of your team’s technical expertise. - Comprehensive Coverage: IntelFinder monitors a wide array of potential threats, including: --- Similar Domain Registration: Mitigates risks such as phishing, brand abuse, and cybersquatting. --- Data Leaks: Detects exposure of sensitive documents, employee credentials from infostealers logs, and source code. --- Rogue Applications: Identifies unauthorized apps that could compromise your brand’s integrity. --- Domain Security: Alerts you to domain hijacking attempts and monitors domain and SSL certificate expiration dates. By choosing IntelFinder, you equip your organization with a unique blend of affordability, accessibility, and extensive threat coverage, ensuring robust protection in today’s dynamic cyber landscape.

IntelFinder Threat Intelligence

IntelFinder Threat Intelligence

Threat Intelligence Platforms

IntelFinder is a SaaS-based customer specific and actionable threat intelligence service. We monitor a variety of sources in order to identify external and internal threats to our customers' brands, business and IT security. For example, we cover: - Similar domain registration (often used for Phishing, BEC fraud, brand abuse, etc.) - Leaked employee credentials - Rogue mobile apps - Leaked source code - Exposed subdomains - Leaked internal documents - Trademark application filing - Domain Hijacking - and more! IntelFinder's mission is to make threat intelligence as accessible as possible. To that end, we've developed the service to be fully automated, self-service and scalable. This design enables us to offer it at a fraction of the cost compared to existing services on the market, which rely on human analysts in their intelligence generation process. The service is available as low as $250/month per brand (on an annual subscription).

    Supply chain risk is no longer just a compliance checkbox. Customers are increasingly expected to understand not only their own external exposure, but also the exposure of the suppliers, vendors, and third parties they rely on. That’s why we’re launching Supply Chain Intelligence in IntelFinder. With this new capability, customers can now monitor third-party suppliers directly from their IntelFinder tenant, alongside their own brands and assets. Each supplier can have its own monitored assets and Subscriptions, allowing customers to track external risks across their broader ecosystem, including: • Exposed supplier infrastructure • Vulnerabilities affecting monitored vendors • Ransomware leak site mentions • Supplier breach reports • Malicious packages and typosquat packages targeting monitored package names Our goal is simple: bring IntelFinder’s affordability, simplicity, and automation-first approach to supply chain security. Supply chain intelligence should not be limited to companies with massive budgets or complex enterprise programs. It should be accessible, practical, and easy to operationalize. This is our biggest IntelFinder update to date, and an important step toward helping organizations see risk beyond their own perimeter. #SupplyChainSecurity #CyberSecurity #ThreatIntelligence #ThirdPartyRisk #BrandProtection #IntelFinder

    IntelFinder Co-Founder Idan Aharoni shares what we've learned implementing the Virtual Analyst.

    Idan Aharoni
    6mo

    Selecting the right AI model is not just about choosing between OpenAI, Claude, Gemini, or others. It is also about choosing the right model within a single provider’s lineup. Many people go straight for the latest and greatest model, but when you want to implement AI at scale, it often makes more sense to start with the least sophisticated model and move up only when needed. A good example is our recent implementation of the Virtual Analyst, an AI agent that reviews and classifies alerts. In this case, we chose GPT-5 nano. The main reason was cost. As a service priced at $3,600 per year per brand, where some brands can generate thousands of alerts depending on their size, scope, and setup, financial feasibility was the main hurdle that had prevented us from using AI at scale. That changed when OpenAI released a model at a price point low enough to make large-scale use practical. At current API pricing, GPT-5 nano costs $0.05 per 1M input tokens. For comparison, GPT-5.4 costs $2.50 per 1M input tokens, and GPT-5.4 nano costs four times more than GPT-5 nano on input pricing. Using more sophisticated models, even when they made business sense, came with dramatically higher costs. Choosing the right model is always a balance between price and performance. After submitting a sample set of alerts, all including screenshots, we analyzed the average input and output token usage for each one. With that, we estimated the cost of running the Virtual Analyst across all alerts currently in the service. The result? Using GPT-5 nano turned out to be feasible, but cheaper than running local models, which was the other option we were considering. In terms of performance, after extensive testing and repeated refinement of the system prompts, we reached a level of accuracy that was satisfactory for production use. In our testing, it also outperformed the local models we evaluated. The main drawback of GPT-5 nano is its limited reasoning ability. Compared to its more capable siblings, nano is far less robust. Writing system prompts for nano feels less like traditional prompting and more like writing logic. In our case, many classification errors came from overly broad reasoning instructions. Because reasoning is more limited, edge cases caused GPT-5 nano to fail when the prompt did not cover them. We realized that adding GPT-5 nano to the alert-generation process was not enough. We also needed an internal workflow for testing, refining, and deploying prompts over time. If you are considering GPT-5 nano because of its cost, having that kind of system in place is highly recommended. Later, when we developed web interaction capabilities using Playwright, GPT-5 nano did not perform well enough for that task, so we moved up to GPT-5 mini instead. Working your way up model capabilities is the best way to find the right balance and avoid overspending. At scale, AI only needs to be good enough for the task at hand. Anything beyond that is unnecessary cost.

    Today, we’re excited to announce the rollout of our enhanced Virtual Analyst. The Virtual Analyst is an AI-driven analysis engine that leverages advanced LLM models to triage alerts, i.e. automatically reviewing newly generated alerts, classifying them as true positives or false positives, and determining their priority. By analyzing the full alert context, including screenshots and visual evidence, the Virtual Analyst helps reduce noise and alert fatigue, save valuable analyst time, and improve signal accuracy. Teams can start safely by enabling suggestive mode to evaluate the Virtual Analyst’s accuracy, then gradually introduce automation where it delivers the most value. Privacy remains a priority. These advanced capabilities are opt-in and disabled by default, and sensitive subscription types such as Leaked Employee Credentials are excluded from AI analysis. The enhanced Virtual Analyst is currently in beta, and we’re actively working with customers and partners to further refine accuracy and capabilities. If you’re interested in seeing how AI can meaningfully improve alert triage and prioritization, we’d love to hear your feedback. #CyberSecurity #BrandProtection #ThreatIntelligence #AI #SecurityOperations #AlertFatigue
